details.biography:
The Broken Anvil · Level 5 - The Journeymen · Seat 4, Ranged

A cheerful gnome alchemist with a bag full of bombs and a home-made zap-gun. Excitable, curious and slightly too fond of explosions; names every bomb and mourns each one a little as she throws it. Grew up in Tariel's workshops; joined the Keepers for the steady supply of interesting things to set on fire.

In a fight

Stay behind the knight; each turn throw a formula and fire the Spark Caster in the same action (Quick Hands). Save the Fire Bombs and Caustic Flasks for the troll.
details.backgroundStory:
Abilities (from the printed sheet)

Quick Hands. Using a formula (throwing or drinking it) can be part of your action: use one AND make one weapon attack (your Spark Caster) with the same action.

Ingenuity Points: 8 a day. Int 3 + level 5. Recover on a full rest. They pay for brewing.

Brew Formula + Efficient Brewing. In downtime, brew formulas you know for 1 Ingenuity Point each (bombs included). You can hold 8 brewed formulas (Int 3 + level 5); extras go inert. You start with 8 brewed.

Known formulas (4). Fire Bomb: thrown, 3d6 fire in a 10ft radius, Reflex DC 15 half. Caustic Flask: thrown at one target, Reflex DC 15 or 1d6 acid each round for 3 rounds. Elixir of Vigour: drink for 1d8+3 temporary HP. Smoke Powder Bomb: thrown, 15ft-radius obscuring cloud (attacks into or through it have Disadvantage).

Spark Caster. Ranged attack out to 60ft at +3, 1d8 force, counts as a magic weapon, once a round.

Tinker's Craft (Int). Build, repair, identify and jury-rig mechanisms and minor magic items: Int check +3, +2 class bonus. Needs your toolkit.

Reliable Craft. Any GM-adjudicated kit effect gives at least +1 to the check or save it affects, or at least 1d6 damage or healing.

Small. Small size: Advantage on Move Silently and stealth checks and on checks to escape a grapple or Restrained; Disadvantage on attacks with Heavy weapons. Darkvision 60ft; speed 25ft.

Gnomish cunning. Advantage on Will saves against magic.

Chosen Expertise: Alchemy. Advantage on Alchemy checks, and on building, repairing or identifying small mechanical devices.

Puzzle-solver. Advantage on Intelligence checks to solve a puzzle, riddle or mechanism under time pressure.

Small and slippery. Advantage on checks to hide or squeeze through tight spaces, despite encumbrance.

Clever Fallback (1/long rest). Reroll one failed Intelligence check (burn 1 Luck for a second use).

Tariel Gnome. Advantage on Charisma checks with human communities, and on trade, commission and small-business checks.

Training. Weapons: dagger, light hammer, hand crossbow, sling.

Toughness (General). +1 Constitution (included), +1 Max HP per level (included), Advantage on Constitution checks.

Steady Aim (Specialist). No Disadvantage on ranged attacks against a target engaged in melee with an ally (Spark Caster and thrown daggers).

Speed, Initiative and HP. Speed: 25ft · Initiative: +2 · HP: d6: 1st level 6 + Con 2 = 8; levels 2-5: 4 x (4 + 2) = 24; Toughness +1 per level = +5. Total 37.

Armour Class on the sheet: 10 + 4 (Cuir Bouille) + 1 (magic) + 2 (Dex; Medium armour, max +2) = 17

Level by Level at a Glance

Class Abilities

1st Level

Tinker's Craft (Intelligence)

  • Effect: The shared skill of building, repairing, identifying, and jury-rigging mechanisms and minor magic items. Bonus to the check scales with level: +1 at 1st, +2 at 5th, +3 at 9th, +4 at 13th, +5 at 17th, +6 at 21st.

Ingenuity Points

  • Effect: A daily pool equal to Intelligence modifier + Artificer level (minimum 1) that fuels your Kit's abilities. Recovers fully on a full rest.
  • Kit Feature (1st): gain the 1st-tier ability from your chosen Kit

Reliable Craft

  • Effect: Whenever a Kit ability's exact effect is left open to GM adjudication (Infuse Item's chosen property, Quickbuild Gadget's specific effect, and similar), it always includes at minimum a flat +1 bonus per 4 Artificer levels (minimum +1) to whatever check or save it affects, or base damage/healing of 1d6 per 4 levels (minimum 1d6) if the effect is damaging or restorative. This is a floor, not a cap — a generous GM ruling can always exceed it, but it never falls below this baseline.

First Creation

  • Effect: You begin play with one item already made — chosen freely from your Kit's Known list in The Artificer's Workshop — with no Ingenuity Point cost and no crafting time spent.
  • An Infuser starts with one item already infused (the infusion lasts as normal and can be renewed the usual way once it ends); a Gadgeteer starts with one gadget already built and ready to use; an Alchemist starts with one formula already brewed and in their pack.
  • A Construct Engineer instead starts with one Modular Chassis mount already installed on their companion at no cost, on top of the companion itself.

Spark Caster

  • Effect: You carry a hand-built repeater that only you can work.
  • As an attack, make a ranged attack out to 60ft with your Base to Hit plus your Intelligence modifier.
  • It deals force damage equal to a Warlock's Eldritch Blast for your level (1d6; 1d8 at 5th, 2d6 at 9th, 2d8 at 13th, 3d6 at 17th, 3d8 at 24th), counts as a magic weapon, and fires once a round even if you gain Extra Attack.

2nd Level

Quick Hands

  • Effect: Using an infused item, gadget or formula can be part of your action: use one and also make one weapon attack or cast one cantrip with the same action.

3rd Level

  • Kit Feature (3rd): gain the 3rd-tier ability from your chosen Kit

4th Level

Salvage

  • Effect: Once per day, spend 10 minutes tinkering to regain Ingenuity Points equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1).

5th Level

  • Kit Feature (5th): gain the 5th-tier ability from your chosen Kit

6th Level

Overclock

  • Effect: Spend 2 extra Ingenuity Points on a damaging or healing Kit effect to roll its dice twice and keep the higher result.

7th Level

  • Kit Feature (7th): gain the 7th-tier ability from your chosen Kit

10th Level

  • Lasting Work: gain the permanent-item-creation ability from your chosen Kit — every Kit can now produce true, lasting magic items rather than only temporary or consumable effects. Until 15th level you can use it only once a month

13th Level

Master Artisan

  • Effect: Your Kit abilities cost 1 fewer Ingenuity Point (minimum 1).

15th Level

  • Intelligence Bonus: permanent +1 Intelligence
  • Lasting Work improves: once a week, as your Kit describes

20th Level

  • Lasting Work improves: you may use your Kit's permanent-creation ability twice per week rather than once (Construct Engineer enhancement limits are unchanged). An Infuser's Permanent Infusion needs materials worth only half the item's value

24th Level

Magnum Opus

  • Effect: Gain the capstone creation unique to your chosen Kit — a singular, legendary work representing the height of your craft.

Kits: Disciplines of Craft

Each kit is an item in the Kits compendium, in the Artificer folder. Drag one onto your character.

Every Artificer shares Tinker's Craft and Ingenuity Points. Your Kit defines exactly what those resources build, from the 1st-level feature through to your Magnum Opus at 24th.

Kit: Infuser

  • You don't build new things — you make old things briefly extraordinary.
  • A sword becomes flame for an hour.
  • A cloak becomes a wing.
  • Everything reverts eventually.
  • Infusers alone among Artificers are trained to work fine enchantment even through a full suit of plate — you are trained in all armour and shields.
  • You also choose one weapon at character creation to gain proficiency in, on top of your normal class weapon list — most Infusers pick whatever they intend to keep permanently enchanted.
  • Kit Feature (1st): Infuse Item: as an action, spend 1 Ingenuity Point to grant a mundane weapon, suit of armour, shield, or tool a temporary magical property from your known list (see Known options in The Artificer's Workshop) for 1 hour per level. Number of items infused at once equals half your level (rounded up).
  • Kit Feature (3rd): Sustained Working: infusions no longer end early if you're knocked unconscious — only duration or Ingenuity spent to cancel ends them.
  • Kit Feature (5th): Layered Infusion: infuse a single item with two properties simultaneously for double the Ingenuity cost.
  • Kit Feature (7th): Reflexive Infusion: for 1 extra Ingenuity Point, infuse an item as part of another action rather than using your whole action.
  • Lasting Work (10th): Lasting Work — Permanent Infusion: as often as Lasting Work allows, spend a full day and appropriate materials to make one infusion permanent on a single item rather than temporary — for example, a blade that keeps Flametongue's fire damage forever, or a shield permanently etched with Ward-Etched's save bonus. The item becomes a true magic item and no longer draws on your Ingenuity Points.
  • Magnum Opus (24th): The Everwork: create a single permanent magic item embodying every infusion property you know simultaneously. Requires a month of uninterrupted work and rare materials the GM determines. Unique — only one Everwork can exist per Artificer.

Kit: Construct Engineer

  • Your companion isn't summoned — it's built, bolted, and wound by hand, and it remembers every repair you've ever made to it.
  • Kit Feature (1st): Construct Companion: build a Small construct companion (d8 Hit Dice equal to your level; AC 14, +1 per four levels; attack bonus equal to the Martial Base to Hit for a level equal to its HD, to a maximum of 24th; saves of half your level, minimum +1; immune to poison, disease and sleep).
  • Its attacks deal +1 damage per four Artificer levels.
  • It acts on your initiative and follows spoken commands.
  • Commanding it is part of your turn and costs nothing; without a command it takes no action.
  • Example chassis — Guardian: Move 30ft, slam (1d8), +1 AC while adjacent to you; Scout: Move 40ft, climb 20ft, bite (1d6), Advantage on Perception; Striker: Move 30ft, blade arm (1d10).
  • If destroyed, it can be rebuilt over a full rest with materials.
  • Kit Feature (3rd): Modular Chassis: swap the construct's weapon mount (Blade Arm, Cannon Arm) or utility mount (Grasping Claw, Lantern Core, Climbing Legs, Alarm Core) during any rest, no cost.
  • Kit Feature (5th): Reinforced Plating: the construct's AC increases by 2 and it gains Resistance 5 to one damage type of your choice, set at creation.
  • Kit Feature (7th): Independent Action: the construct can act on its own initiative count and no longer requires your command each round to take a basic action (attack nearest enemy, defend, retrieve).
  • Lasting Work (10th): Lasting Work — True Construct: spend a full day and appropriate materials to permanently upgrade your companion's chassis — each upgrade gives it 2 more Hit Dice and one permanent magical enhancement (flight, invisibility on command, a breath weapon dealing elemental damage, or similar), GM-approved. It can take one upgrade at 10th level and a second at 20th; replacing an enhancement later adds no Hit Dice.
  • Magnum Opus (24th): The Masterwork Automaton: your companion undergoes a final transformation — +4 HD, it gains a second attack, and it can cast one Wizard spell of 3rd level or lower, chosen when the Opus is finished, whenever you spend 2 Ingenuity Points per spell level. Requires a month of uninterrupted work and rare materials the GM determines.

Kit: Gadgeteer

  • Pockets full of things that shouldn't work as well as they do. You're never quite out of options, just out of Ingenuity Points.
  • Kit Feature (1st): Quickbuild Gadget: as an action, spend 1 Ingenuity Point to produce a single-use gadget from your known list (smoke bomb, grapnel line, shock glove, flash powder, etc.) — effect equivalent to a 1st-level spell or utility effect, GM-adjudicated case by case. You can hold built gadgets equal to your Intelligence modifier + half your Artificer level; extras go inert.
  • Kit Feature (3rd): Reusable Chassis: one gadget of your choice (a Grapnel Line or Shock Glove are popular picks) becomes reusable rather than single-use, recharging on a full rest instead of costing Ingenuity each use.
  • Kit Feature (5th): Rapid Deployment: quickbuilding a gadget no longer requires an action if done in response to being surprised or ambushed; it costs 1 extra Ingenuity Point.
  • Kit Feature (7th): Expanded Toolkit: you know two more gadgets than your known options allow, and you can hold one more built gadget at a time.
  • Lasting Work (10th): Lasting Work — Signature Device: as often as Lasting Work allows, spend a full day and appropriate materials to build one permanent, unique gadget with a lasting magical effect (not single-use) tailored to your specifications with the GM — a boot that deploys Rapid Ascent for free once per day, a ring that emits Smoke Bomb's cloud on command, or a glove with an always-on Shock Glove charge are all typical examples.
  • Magnum Opus (24th): The Impossible Case: a portable kit containing a permanent version of every gadget you've ever built, foldable into a case the size of a book. Requires a month of uninterrupted work and rare materials the GM determines.

Kit: Alchemist

  • Less about the one perfect tool, more about the shelf of forty imperfect ones. Something in the bag always does the job.
  • Kit Feature (1st): Brew Formula: during downtime, brew potions, bombs, and elixirs from your known formula list, each formula costs 1 Ingenuity Point to brew (2 for a damaging one) and persists until used. You can hold brewed formulas equal to your Intelligence modifier + your Artificer level; extras go inert.
  • Kit Feature (3rd): Efficient Brewing: formulas cost 1 less Ingenuity Point to brew (minimum 1).
  • Kit Feature (5th): Combat Alchemy: brew a single formula on the spot as an action at double the normal Ingenuity cost.
  • Kit Feature (7th): Volatile Mastery: your bombs and harmful formulas deal an additional die of damage.
  • Lasting Work (10th): Lasting Work — Perfected Formula: as often as Lasting Work allows, spend a full day and appropriate materials to perfect one formula into a permanent-effect item (a ring that continuously radiates Draught of Clarity's protection, a self-refilling flask of Elixir of Vigour, or a blade permanently coated with Caustic Flask's acid) rather than a consumable.
  • Magnum Opus (24th): The Panacea: brew a single legendary elixir capable of curing any one affliction, condition, or injury when drunk — including things no ordinary Restoration-tier magic touches.
  • One dose only, ever, per Artificer.
  • Requires a month of uninterrupted work and rare materials the GM determines.

Crafting & Materials

  • Deliberately kept loose rather than a rigid shopping list — where you are determines how crafting actually works, and the GM adjudicates specifics on the fly. This is the guide, not a strict table.

Large Towns & Cities

  • A proper market means materials are simply available.
  • Pay a gold cost (the GM sets this based on the effect's power, roughly in line with an equivalent item's price in the Shopkeeper's Catalogue) and acquire what you need with no search required.
  • This is the default assumption for most crafting downtime spent in Mournas or any similarly-sized settlement.

Remote Villages & Small Settlements

  • Limited stock.
  • Common materials are usually available, sometimes at a markup; anything specific or unusual has to be special-ordered (taking real downtime to arrive) or sought out personally.
  • The GM may call for a Persuasion or relevant Skill check to track down an uncommon component through local contacts.

Wilderness & Frontier

  • No market at all. Materials have to be foraged, scavenged, or hunted directly — the GM determines what's plausible to find in the area and calls for an appropriate check (Survival, Nature-adjacent Skills, or a relevant skill) before the material is actually in hand.

Kit Variance

  • Alchemist: The most flexible Kit by far — herbs, venoms, fungi, and minerals can genuinely be foraged in the wild with a successful Survival or Herbalism-type check, making Alchemists far less dependent on a market than the other three Kits.
  • Infuser, Construct Engineer, Gadgeteer: Lean on manufactured components — refined metal, gears, glass, wiring — that are difficult or impossible to improvise from raw wilderness materials. These three Kits are much more reliant on a proper town or city market, or a well-stocked workshop back home, to actually craft anything substantial.

Tools Required

  • Regardless of location or Kit, an Artificer cannot use Tinker's Craft or any Kit crafting feature without their tools in hand — the toolkit matching their Kit (see Starting Equipment & Gear) or an equivalent toolset. No tools, no crafting, no matter how good the market is.

The Artificer's Workshop

  • The full catalogue of ready-to-use options for each Kit, plus guidelines for designing something new with your GM.
  • Known options: you know a number of options from your Kit's list equal to 2 + half your Artificer level (rounded down).
  • Each time you gain a level you may swap one known option for another.
  • A custom design agreed with your GM takes one known option, and the guidelines below are the benchmark for it.

Infuser: Known Infusions

  • Flametongue — Weapon deals an additional 1d6 fire damage on a hit
  • Frostbrand — Weapon deals an additional 1d6 cold damage on a hit, and the target's speed is halved for 1 round
  • Shockgrip — Weapon deals an additional 1d6 lightning damage on a hit
  • Guardian Plating — Armour grants +2 AC
  • Featherweight — The item's slot cost is halved (round up) for the duration; if worn armour, its Strength requirement is waived
  • Returning Throw — A thrown weapon flies back to your hand immediately after the attack resolves
  • Ward-Etched — A shield adds +1 to all saving throws in addition to its normal AC bonus
  • Glowing Ward — The item sheds light in a 30ft radius, and its wielder gains Advantage on saves vs fear
  • Silent Step — Armour or boots grant Advantage on Move Silently checks
  • Bloodhound's Edge — A weapon grants Advantage on checks to track a creature it has damaged within the last 24 hours
  • Reach Extended — A melee weapon's reach increases by 5ft
  • Truth-Etched — A tool grants Advantage on checks to detect forgeries, lies, or magical disguises while in use
  • Deadweight — A weapon adds +2 damage against a target that is Restrained, Prone, or otherwise immobilised

Designing a Custom Infusion

  • Benchmark: A single Infusion should do roughly one of the following — add a damage die (1d6 of a chosen type), grant a flat +1 or +2 to one specific roll or AC, provide a narrow at-will utility effect (light, minor detection, a movement quirk), or impose a specific condition on a hit (halved speed, Disadvantage on the target's next save). Avoid stacking two of these into one Infusion unless it's the result of Layered Infusion (5th level) or Lasting Work.

Construct Engineer: Known Chassis Mods

  • Blade Arm (weapon mount) — 1d8 slashing melee attack
  • Cannon Arm (weapon mount) — 1d6 force damage, 30ft range
  • Piercer Arm (weapon mount) — 1d6 piercing melee attack, ignores 2 points of the target's armour
  • Grasping Claw (utility mount) — Advantage on grapple attempts; can retrieve small objects at your command
  • Lantern Core (utility mount) — Sheds light in a 30ft radius, shutterable on command
  • Climbing Legs (utility mount) — Climb speed equal to normal move speed
  • Alarm Core (utility mount) — The construct cannot be surprised while active and alerts you the instant it's triggered or attacked
  • Vocal Mimic (utility mount) — The construct can repeat up to one sentence of speech it has heard, in the speaker's own voice
  • Reinforced Chassis (passive) — +2 to the construct's current HD total
  • Balanced Frame (passive) — The construct gains +1 to its AC
  • Recall Ward (passive) — You can call the construct to your side from anywhere within 1 mile with a spoken word
  • Storage Cavity (utility mount) — The construct has a hidden compartment holding up to 4 slots' worth of items
  • Mounts and passives: a construct carries one weapon mount and one utility mount, swapped during a rest (see Modular Chassis).
  • Passives are installed during a rest and count as known options.
  • A construct holds one passive, plus one more at 5th, 10th, 15th and 20th level.
  • Each passive can be installed only once, and removing and reinstalling Reinforced Chassis adds no further Hit Dice.

Designing a Custom Mount

  • Benchmark: A weapon mount should deal damage in line with a simple one-handed weapon (1d6-1d8), scaled by attack type rather than by size.
  • A utility mount should grant one clear non-combat capability (movement, detection, storage, communication) rather than a combat bonus — if it starts granting damage or AC, it's a weapon mount or passive instead.
  • A passive mod should be a small, permanent numeric bump (+1 to +2) to one stat, never a whole new capability.

Gadgeteer: Known Gadgets

  • Smoke Bomb — Creates a 15ft radius heavily obscured area for 1 minute
  • Shock Glove — Melee touch attack — 1d6 lightning damage, target saves or is stunned 1 round
  • Grapnel Line — Instantly close a 30ft gap to a solid anchor point, or pull a Medium or smaller target 15ft towards you
  • Flash Powder — 10ft radius burst — creatures save or are blinded for 1 round
  • Adhesive Charge — Thrown — target is Restrained until they break free with a Strength check
  • Distraction Decoy — A small mechanical decoy moves and makes noise on your command for 1 minute
  • Rapid Ascent Boots — One use — gain a 20ft vertical or horizontal jump-assisted burst of movement
  • Noisemaker Dart — Thrown to a point within 30ft — creates a loud, distinct noise there, no damage
  • Caltrop Scatter — Covers a 10ft square with caltrops — creatures entering without care take 1d4 damage and have their speed halved for the round
  • Pocket Ram — One use — a spring-loaded ram deals 1d8 damage to a door, lock, or barricade
  • Glass-Cutter Ring — Silently cuts a hole in glass or thin material large enough to reach through
  • Signal Flare — Fired into the air — visible for 1 mile in clear conditions, in a colour of your choosing

Designing a Custom Gadget

  • Benchmark: A combat gadget should land somewhere around a 1st-level spell's worth of effect — a single damage instance (1d6-2d6), a single save-or-suffer condition lasting 1 round, or an area effect no larger than 15ft radius. A utility gadget should solve one specific problem (noise, light, a locked door, a gap to cross) rather than several at once, and should almost always be single-use unless upgraded by Reusable Chassis.

Alchemist: Known Formulas

  • Fire Bomb — Thrown — 2d6 fire damage, plus 1d6 per five Artificer levels, in a 10ft radius, Reflex save for half
  • Elixir of Vigour — Drink to gain temporary HP equal to 1d8 + Intelligence modifier
  • Caustic Flask — Thrown — target saves or takes 1d6 acid damage per round for 3 rounds
  • Draught of Clarity — Drink for Advantage on your next saving throw vs a mind-affecting effect within 1 hour
  • Smoke Powder Bomb — Thrown — creates a 15ft radius obscuring cloud
  • Sovereign Glue — Bonds two objects together permanently, or until dissolved by a specific solvent
  • Universal Solvent — A few drops dissolve any adhesive on contact, including your own Sovereign Glue
  • Draught of Steady Hands — Drink for Advantage on your next Dexterity-based check within 1 hour
  • Numbing Salve — Applied to a wound — the recipient ignores the effects of 1 point of exhaustion for 1 hour
  • Choking Gas Vial — Thrown — 10ft radius, creatures save or are unable to speak or cast verbal spells for 1 round
  • Quickfoam — Thrown at a fire or flammable area — extinguishes flames in a 10ft radius instantly
  • Reagent of Revealing — A few drops on a surface reveal invisible writing, residue, or a recently-handled object's last handler (GM discretion)

Designing a Custom Formula

  • Benchmark: A thrown or drunk formula should land at roughly a 1st-level spell's potency — 2d6 damage in a small area, a single round of a save-or-suffer condition, or a flat, narrow buff (Advantage on one specific roll type, or temporary HP equal to a small die plus Intelligence modifier). Formulas that grant information or utility (detection, identification, minor restoration) should require a genuine cost — a rare ingredient, a full round to apply, or a limited number of uses — rather than being free and repeatable.

Less about the one perfect tool, more about the shelf of forty imperfect ones. Something in the bag always does the job.

  • Brew Formula (1st): During downtime, brew potions, bombs, and elixirs from your known formula list, each formula costs 1 Ingenuity Point to brew (2 for a damaging one) and persists until used. You can hold brewed formulas equal to your Intelligence modifier + your Artificer level; extras go inert.
  • Efficient Brewing (3rd): Formulas cost 1 less Ingenuity Point to brew (minimum 1).
  • Combat Alchemy (5th): Brew a single formula on the spot as an action at double the normal Ingenuity cost.
  • Volatile Mastery (7th): Your bombs and harmful formulas deal an additional die of damage.
  • Lasting Work: Perfected Formula (10th): As often as Lasting Work allows, spend a full day and appropriate materials to perfect one formula into a permanent-effect item (a ring that continuously radiates Draught of Clarity's protection, a self-refilling flask of Elixir of Vigour, or a blade permanently coated with Caustic Flask's acid) rather than a consumable.
  • Magnum Opus: The Panacea (24th): Brew a single legendary elixir capable of curing any one affliction, condition, or injury when drunk — including things no ordinary Restoration-tier magic touches.
  • One dose only, ever, per Artificer.
  • Requires a month of uninterrupted work and rare materials the GM determines.

Known Formulas

  • Fire Bomb — Thrown — 2d6 fire damage, plus 1d6 per five Artificer levels, in a 10ft radius, Reflex save for half
  • Elixir of Vigour — Drink to gain temporary HP equal to 1d8 + Intelligence modifier
  • Caustic Flask — Thrown — target saves or takes 1d6 acid damage per round for 3 rounds
  • Draught of Clarity — Drink for Advantage on your next saving throw vs a mind-affecting effect within 1 hour
  • Smoke Powder Bomb — Thrown — creates a 15ft radius obscuring cloud
  • Sovereign Glue — Bonds two objects together permanently, or until dissolved by a specific solvent
  • Universal Solvent — A few drops dissolve any adhesive on contact, including your own Sovereign Glue
  • Draught of Steady Hands — Drink for Advantage on your next Dexterity-based check within 1 hour
  • Numbing Salve — Applied to a wound — the recipient ignores the effects of 1 point of exhaustion for 1 hour
  • Choking Gas Vial — Thrown — 10ft radius, creatures save or are unable to speak or cast verbal spells for 1 round
  • Quickfoam — Thrown at a fire or flammable area — extinguishes flames in a 10ft radius instantly
  • Reagent of Revealing — A few drops on a surface reveal invisible writing, residue, or a recently-handled object's last handler (GM discretion)

Designing a Custom Formula

  • Benchmark: A thrown or drunk formula should land at roughly a 1st-level spell's potency — 2d6 damage in a small area, a single round of a save-or-suffer condition, or a flat, narrow buff (Advantage on one specific roll type, or temporary HP equal to a small die plus Intelligence modifier). Formulas that grant information or utility (detection, identification, minor restoration) should require a genuine cost — a rare ingredient, a full round to apply, or a limited number of uses — rather than being free and repeatable.
